name: notifications_kind_decode
why: KIND_CD is decoded through CODES NOTIF_KIND; the source holds an integer and the target a string, so no canonicalization rule can compare them.
source_sql: SELECT n.id AS "id", NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(n.kind_cd) || ')') AS "kind" FROM notifications n LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'NOTIF_KIND' AND c.code_val = n.kind_cd

name: notifications_kind_counts
why: The decoded kind as a distribution, so an extra or missing notification shows up as a count, not just a row diff.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(n.kind_cd) || ')') AS "kind", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM notifications n LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'NOTIF_KIND' AND c.code_val = n.kind_cd GROUP BY NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(n.kind_cd) || ')')

name: notifications_idempotency_key_unique
why: (tenantId, kind, sentAt) is the unique index and the reload idempotency key; it must be unique on both sides.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "groups", MAX(cnt) AS "maxPerKey" FROM (SELECT n.tenant_id, n.kind_cd, n.sent_at, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM notifications n GROUP BY n.tenant_id, n.kind_cd, n.sent_at)

name: credit_notes_outstanding_by_tenant
why: The app-level question this collection answers: outstanding credit per tenant. Money totals compare to 0.01 per the tolerance record.
source_sql: SELECT tenant_id AS "tenantId", TO_CHAR(ROUND(SUM(remaining_amount) * 100), 'FM999999999990') AS "remainingCents", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM credit_notes GROUP BY tenant_id

name: credit_notes_issued_month
why: ISSUED_ON is a DATE; grouping by month proves the UTC conversion did not shift a note across a boundary.
source_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(issued_on, 'YYYY-MM') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM credit_notes GROUP BY TO_CHAR(issued_on, 'YYYY-MM')

name: audit_log_empty
why: BILLING_AUDIT_LOG is empty at source; the correct target is an empty collection, and the TTL index deletes nothing at migration time. Both sides return zero rows, which is the assertion.
source_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(log_id) AS "id", TO_CHAR(logged_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') AS "loggedAt", module AS "module" FROM billing_audit_log
